text.p: Serbian police said on Monday they had arrested the alleged head of an ethnic Albanian "terrorist" group plotting armed rebellion in the troubled province of Kosovo, state media reported.
The police said Avni Klinaku, 31, was arrested on Sunday along with several other members of the "National Movement for the Liberation of Kosovo".
The shadowy organisation claimed responsibility for a series of attacks on Serbian police in Kosovo last year but no details of its structure or origin have emerged.
The interior ministry accused Klinaku of organising "terrorist groups" with the aim of overthrowing Serbian rule in the predominantly Albanian southern province, the Yugoslav Tanjug news agency said.
"A search of their quarters discovered arms and ammunition of various calibres, drawings and plans for attacks on facilities, and other means for carrying out terrorist actions," the ministry said.
The arrests came amid a deepening political crisis in Serbia after 10 weeks of opposition protests demanding that the ruling Socialists recognise results of municipal elections.
State media have accused the opposition of attempting to foment unrest among ethnic Albanians in Kosovo.

The opposition denies the charge and has accused authorities of trying to divert attention from the election protests, which pose an unprecedented challenge to President Slobodan Milosevic's nine-year rule.
Police announced the arrest after a car-bombing this month critically injured the Serbian rector of Pristina university.
State-controlled television broadcast allegations by the Serbian mayor of Pristina, Kosovo's provincial capital, that opposition leaders had orchestrated the incident to destabilise the country.
Milosevic stripped Kosovo of its autonomous status in 1989 to concentrate power in his hands and appeal to Serbian nationalism inside the former Yugoslav federation.
Belgrade authorities have accused ethnic Albanian leaders of trying to secede from Serbia.
Human rights workers have condemned Serbian police for rampant abuses against ethnic Albanian activists who support self-rule for the 90 percent Albanian majority.
